actions.justification: Mandatory action with 10-minute deadline. Patient has critical vitals: HR 116, RR 34, SpO2 82%, BP 152/94, Temp 38.2°C — full vital signs assessment must be completed immediately.

Mandatory action. Patient has severe respiratory compromise (SpO2 82%, RR 34, unable to complete sentences) requiring immediate respiratory status assessment to guide therapy including NIV eligibility.

Mandatory per GOLD guidelines for severe COPD exacerbation. ABG is essential to assess degree of hypoxemia, hypercapnia, and respiratory acidosis, which will guide oxygen therapy targets and NIV initiation.
MANDATORY action per current phase deadline (60 min). Chest X-ray is essential to identify precipitating causes of COPD exacerbation (pneumonia, pneumothorax, pulmonary edema) and guide management.
GOLD guideline mandates bronchodilator within 30 minutes for severe COPD exacerbation. Patient has RR 34, SpO2 82%, severe dyspnea — immediate bronchodilator therapy is critical.

Patient is confused, which is a sign of hypercapnic respiratory failure. Mental status assessment is needed to determine NIV eligibility and severity of encephalopathy, and to monitor for deterioration requiring intubation.
GOLD guideline mandates systemic corticosteroids for severe COPD exacerbation to reduce inflammation and speed recovery. This is a mandatory action not yet completed.
GOLD guideline mandates antibiotics for severe COPD exacerbation, especially with signs of infection (Temp 38.2°C). Mandatory action not yet completed.

GOLD guideline mandates assessment of NIV eligibility in severe COPD exacerbation. Patient has SpO2 82%, RR 34, confusion — classic indications for NIV consideration. This is a mandatory action not yet completed.

SpO2 is critically low at 82%. Supplemental oxygen is urgently needed. For COPD patients, controlled low-flow oxygen targeting SpO2 88-92% is appropriate to avoid hypercapnic drive suppression. ABG already ordered to monitor CO2 levels.
CBC will help identify infection severity (leukocytosis), anemia contributing to hypoxia, and polycythemia common in GOLD stage 4 COPD/cor pulmonale.

BMP will assess electrolytes, renal function, and bicarbonate (to evaluate chronic CO2 retention and metabolic compensation) — important for managing this patient with cor pulmonale and severe exacerbation.
Procalcitonin helps differentiate bacterial from viral etiology in COPD exacerbation, guiding antibiotic stewardship. Patient has fever (38.2°C) suggesting possible infectious trigger.
Sputum culture identifies causative organism to guide antibiotic therapy. Antibiotics already initiated but culture should be obtained to ensure appropriate coverage.

Patient has severe COPD exacerbation (SpO2 82%, RR 34, confusion) with GOLD Stage 4 COPD and cor pulmonale — complex case requiring pulmonology expertise, particularly for NIV management decisions and escalation planning.
Patient has fever 38.2°C with severe COPD exacerbation; blood cultures help identify bacteremia/infectious trigger and guide antibiotic therapy.
Patient has confusion, tachycardia HR 116, and severe hypoxia (SpO2 82%); lactate helps assess for tissue hypoperfusion/sepsis component and guides resuscitation.
Severe refractory hypoxia with confusion warrants CT chest to exclude pulmonary embolism (common complication in COPD) and other structural causes not visible on plain X-ray.
